$comment: Shared value definitions. Definition names are unique across every file in this directory because the generator merges all $defs into one namespace.

Id.description: Record identifier. The character set is the OpenAPI component-key set, so an id is usable as a JSON Pointer segment, a schema component name and a file-name stem without escaping.

QualifiedId.description: A record id, optionally prefixed by a published-contract id and a colon to reference a record inside a pinned published contract.

Name.description: Member name (property, parameter, column, alternative). The character set is the intersection of SQL, PowerShell, C# and TypeScript identifiers.

Alias.description: Accountable owner or authority, named by team or role alias, never by a person.

Text.description: Non-empty prose. An unknown value is recorded as an unknown record, never as an empty string.

ContractVersion.description: Contract version of a versioned record. Distinct from the model format version, the configuration version and the record revision.

Revision.description: Revision of an authored knowledge record; incremented when its meaning changes.

Hash.description: SHA-256 digest of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace) or of the exact bytes of a file.

Duration.description: ISO 8601 duration, for example PT30S or P7D.

RelativePath.description: Repository-relative path with forward slashes. Absolute paths, drive letters, backslashes and '..' segments are rejected.

MachinePath.description: An absolute path on the local machine: a drive letter or a root slash, never a network share and never a '..' segment. Only a machine-local record that is never committed, projected or signed holds one, because the location differs on every machine; a path that names repository content is a RelativePath.

estimate.description: True when the value is an estimate rather than a measurement.

Basis.description: Epistemic status of a claim. 'accepted' is honoured only when a trusted acceptance record covers the claim; the stored word alone grants nothing.

SourceRef.description: Identifies the document or artifact a claim comes from, and the revision or retrieval context that pins it.

locator.description: Section, line or anchor inside the source.

RecordRef.description: Typed reference to a model record. A property is referenced as '<typeId>.<propertyName>'; an element of a composite-keyed collection, such as an edge, by its key values joined with '|', for example '<from>|<to>|<kind>'.

TaskClass.description: Class of work whose prerequisites differ.

Maturity.description: Contract maturity, distinct from task phase and from deployment state.

EnvironmentKind.description: The kind of environment a check executes in: the local process, a disposable fixture the run owns, or a designated ci, test, staging or production environment.

CheckResult.description: Result of one executed check. NOT_APPLICABLE requires a recorded justification.

UnavailableCause.description: The typed cause of an UNKNOWN result: what kept a check from establishing PASS or FAIL. 'tool-absent', 'version-policy', 'unreadable', 'crashed' and 'timeout' name the tool or its run; 'connection' and 'login' the database it had to reach; 'cancelled' a run cancelled before the check finished; 'insufficient-resources' a fixture that cannot run inside the run budgets, which never raises a limit; and 'provider-blocked' a provider that trusted configuration or the service permissions do not let the run start. A required UNKNOWN never qualifies.

LifecyclePhase.description: A resource-lifecycle phase of a disposable SQL run, in the order a run passes through them: preflight validates the tools, capabilities, free disk, permissions and trusted scripts; reserve takes the lease and journals the allocation intent; start starts the owned engine; prepare creates the run's databases; execute runs the checks; capture persists their outcomes outside the disposable directory; quiesce stops remaining work; remove-databases drops the run's databases; stop stops the engine; and release removes the owned instance, restores the service startup state and releases the lease. RunPhase is the separate stage a run handle reports.

CleanupState.description: The state of a run's cleanup. 'clean' holds only when every owned database, file, process and service is removed, stopped or restored and nothing owned is residual; 'failed' keeps the allocation journal so that recovery can settle what is residual.

CleanupOutcome.description: The outcome of one cleanup step or owned resource: 'done' when it was cancelled, stopped, removed or restored as its kind requires, 'not-needed' when there was nothing to do, and 'failed' otherwise.

ProviderKind.description: The kind of a disposable SQL provider. 'localdb' is a LocalDB instance the run creates and owns; 'developer-service' is a dedicated Developer edition service, provisioned separately and used only for development and testing, which a run starts and stops and never takes over while it already runs.

Dimension.description: Compatibility dimension a change is assessed in.

ConcernId.description: Identifier of an applicable design concern from the behavior profile, for example 'operation.idempotency'.

NotApplicable.description: Justified exclusion of an applicable concern for one record.

Signature.description: Detached Ed25519 signature over the canonical JSON of the enclosing record with its 'signature' member removed.

ModelId.description: Declared stable identity of a persistent model, the same wherever its repository is checked out; never a path.

ModelKind.description: What a model owns: a composition owns system outcomes, cross-component constraints, interaction workflows, boundary agreements, integration scenarios and release assembly; an implementation owns its claimed source roots and their contracts; a mixed model owns explicitly listed local implementation roots plus composition records.

CommitId.description: A Git commit id in lower-case hexadecimal, abbreviated or full.

RecordAddress.description: The address of a record owned by one model: the owning model's id, the record kind and the record id. Another model's record resolves only through that model's published bundle.

ResolvedReference.description: A record address resolved against one exact published bundle, naming that bundle's digest.

ContractPin.description: An exact pin of immutable published content. A version alone does not identify content; the digest and the source commit do.

digest.description: Hash of the canonical JSON of the bundle's content.

schemaVersion.description: Model format version of the content.

sourceCommit.description: The commit the bundle was published from.

ProcessIdentity.description: A process named by its id and its creation time. An operating system reuses process ids, so a process with the same id and another creation time is a different process and is never acted on as the owner.
